packs.title: River, Gardens and Nature
packs.promise: Explore Fort Myers through separate history, art, park and nature outings.

q.s: Turn an exhibit observation into a testable question.
st: Choose one current IMAG science or history exhibit from a paid visit or the center's official exhibit page.
Record one thing the exhibit actually shows or describes.
Ask a question that could be tested or checked using that evidence; separate what you saw from your guess.

q.s: Make a two-part study of outdoor art and setting.
st: Check the Alliance's current ArtsPark construction and open-route notices.
From an open public area or official ArtsPark images, select an artwork form and one landscape form.
Sketch or describe how their outlines differ; do not enter work zones.

q.s: Collect three kinds of park edge.
st: Choose an open walking route; the train, rentals and gardens may have separate schedules.
Record a planting edge, a path edge and a recreation or rail feature from public space.
Arrange those three observations into a tiny map of how people use the park.

packs.title: River District on Foot
packs.promise: Follow connected River District spaces, art and civic stories on foot.

q.s: Read the park's edge without stepping toward the water.
st: Use an open park path and choose a comfortable place back from the river edge.
Compare one shaded or planted feature with one long river view.
Describe where you would pause or turn back if an event, heat or rain changes the route.

q.s: Find signs of an older storefront's new role.
st: From the public sidewalk or an open visit, find a facade material or shape the shop identifies in its history.
Find one present-day retail or art-use cue without buying anything.
Record how the two clues show change over time rather than guessing an object's age.

q.s: Use a library to build a small question trail.
st: Check library hours, or use the official library branch page and catalog from anywhere.
Choose three subject areas or resources that could help explore one Fort Myers question.
Put them in a useful reading order, naming what each might help verify rather than inventing an answer.
